newsitem.title: FRANCE: Club Med shares slump on profit outlook.
newsitem.headline: Club Med shares slump on profit outlook.

text.p: The stock of French resort company Club Mediterranee plummeted Wednesday after the group said weak vacation spending would hurt its peak season results.
After an early trading suspension triggered by a drove of sell orders, the stock tumbled nearly 20 percent to a year low before creeping back to close at 329 francs, down 17.3 percent.

The group said Tuesday evening that it expected flat pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit for the second half of its fiscal year, which runs to Oct. 31. Last year's second half pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit was 25 million francs ($4.85 million).
"The overall business climate in continental Europe has exacerbated the tendency of clients to seek out less expensive packages, particularly in the latter part of the summer," it said.
Brokerage houses slashed their earnings forecasts for the group and recommendations on the stock.
"Their major market is in a spending recession," said Paribas Capital Markets analyst Nigel Reed. He said French consumers, unnerved by record unemployment rates, were spending less on vacations.
The result is that Club Med's new lower priced Club Aquarius resorts are faring better than the more expensive Club Med "vacation villages," eroding the group's profit margins.
The group is counting on an expansion in Asia, where consumers are beginning to feel more affluent, particularly in southeast Asia, to ensure long-term profit growth.
It plans to establish around 20 resorts in Asia by the year 2000 and increase the number of visitors to two million. It now has 102 "vacation villages" drawing 1.3 million visitors a year.

The group, which pioneered the all-inclusive holiday in which vacationers pay a set price for food, lodging and entertainment, has been struggling to recover from a severe slump in its business in the early 1990s.

Although its net attributable profit in 1994/95 of 169 million francs was a sharp improvement over the prior year's 94 million ($32.8 million) profit, it was dented by the impact on Club Med of the French nuclear testing last year in the Pacific.
